name: svg-follow-scroll

frames.best_why: All three headline lines are visible with a rich loop of green stroke drawing beside them.

tagline: A lime scribble sweeps across the page and draws itself as you scroll.
summary: A long hero section where scrolling progressively draws a bright green, looping line across the screen while the headline moves up and a dark title panel slides in.
appearance: A large white three-line headline sits centred-left on black with a small grey hint beneath. To its right a thick lime-green line loops in loose scribbles, with parts still undrawn.
behaviour: As the page scrolls the line extends further along its fixed path, revealing loops and long sweeps, while the headline slides up and out and a dark panel with the event title rises into view.
demo_content: Headline 'The Stroke That follows the Scroll Progress' and a 'Design week' panel.
search_phrases: line that draws itself on scroll
scribble path reveals as page scrolls
use_when: A long marketing page wants a hand-drawn line that ties its sections together as the visitor scrolls.
avoid_when: It is pinned inside a 350vh section, so it needs a long page and leaves big empty stretches on short screens.
customise: Nothing is exposed as props: the headline copy, event panel and the lime SVG path are hardcoded and must be edited in the file.
weight_why: One SVG path driven by a single scroll motion value.

a11y.note: The decorative SVG has no title and no reduced-motion path, and the drawn line is purely visual.

issues: The green line runs through the headline, so parts of the text sit on top of the stroke.
Frames 5 and 6 show only the green line, so the hero copy leaves before the stroke finishes.
polish_why: The scroll-linked drawing is striking and smooth; the line crossing the type muddies it.
title: SVG Follow Scroll
